items.text: Use InnoDB and explicit primary keys.
Version schema migrations and test rollback or roll-forward paths.
Encrypt connections and use least-privilege database accounts.
Test point-in-time recovery from real backups.
Monitor replication lag, lock waits, disk headroom, and slow queries.
Keep client retries bounded and make retried writes idempotent.
Application logic does not treat replicas as immediately consistent.
Indexes have measured write, memory, and storage costs.
Application connection pools have explicit upper bounds.
Schema and bulk-data changes avoid long-running transactions.
Recovery does not rely on replication as a backup.
Configuration values are verified against the actual workload.
